note:
The household of Elizabeth Weaver, widow and wine merchant, with her two daughters, her sister and two servants at 2 Park Terrace (#242) on the 1891 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. None of the six was in the record, and 2 Park Terrace held only 1921, so 1891 is free.

A widow carrying on a wine merchant's business in her own name is worth noticing; the return gives her the trade outright, not as a relict or an assistant. She had left the house by 1894, when Wright's Directory prints Edward M. C. Harvey, barrister, at number 2, and Samuel Lowater, hosiery manufacturer, there in 1898-99.

Ann Bellamy is the head's sister. The surname first read Bellanug from the index and was corrected by A. Hagues from the schedule. A sister carrying a different surname would follow if Weaver is Elizabeth's married name and Bellamy her maiden one, but the return does not say so and no maiden name is recorded on that inference. She is not joined to Ethel Francis Bellamy (#744, born 1882), the only Bellamy in the record, a servant at 2 South Road in 1911. The two daughters are given no occupation on the return, so none is entered. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 2 Park Terrace, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95, page 107 (Leicester Special Collections id 164613); 1898-99, page 115 (id 165291).
